_comment: Vendor-neutral registry of the coding practices this project promotes. This is DATA read BY PATH (json.load), never imported as a library — the 3.6-safe gate scripts/check_structure.py, the advisory scripts/check_practices.py, and the agents/practice_refactor/ doer all consume it the same way check_H reads project.json. No provider/vendor is baked into check LOGIC; every provider/tensor token lives here as data (CONVENTIONS section 18). Adding/retiring a practice is a data edit here plus its mechanism; enabling a domain profile is a flag in project.json practices.profiles (NOT here — defining a profile is not enabling it). Every entry carries `subject` ("code" | "docs" — what the practice is ABOUT; scripts/check_practices.py reads only code) and `enforced_by`, a list of mechanism references in a closed grammar (check:<LETTER> | script:<path> | test:<path> | make:<target> | doc:<path>[ §N] | ruff:<CODE> | mypy:<flag>) that check_structure.py check_T resolves — a practice cannot claim a mechanism that does not exist.

rulesets._comment: The concrete lint/type rulesets that carry the 'gate' tier. Mirrors, in DATA, what pyproject.toml enables — check_structure.py check_M reads this to prove pyproject cannot silently LOOSEN the declared policy (a declared extend_select family missing, a mypy flag off, or a 'deferred' family silently selected is an error). Slice 5 widened it: every extend_select family below was measured at zero current violations (pure future-protection), and mypy went full-strict (backlog was 3, now fixed).

deferred._comment: DELIBERATE house-style policy, NOT temporary debt: each fights a chosen convention, so it stays off permanently. check_M errs if any is silently selected in pyproject.
deferred.UP: house style is %-formatting (UP031 would rewrite ~19 sites to f-strings); the 3.6-safe checks in scripts/ require %-formatting anyway
deferred.RUF100: intentional `# noqa: S310` etc. read as unused until the S (bandit) family is selected, which we don't

per_file_ignores._comment: Declared mirror of [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]. Pass 3 widened `make lint-py` from `src tests` to every CODE_ROOT, which surfaced 41 T201 print() sites — all of them process entrypoints writing to stdout, the same carve-out src/app/** already had. Named per file wherever the root also holds library code; scripts/ takes a glob because every print() there is inside a main() and nothing in src/ imports it. check_M ENFORCES this key: a per-file-ignore in pyproject.toml that is not declared here, or that ignores a code this does not list for it, is an error (the previously unread declaration was the widest hole in the parity gate — one `"**/*.py"` line could silence a family corpus-wide).

mypy._comment: `flags` is what check_M enforces at the [tool.mypy] level and is unchanged: strict stays ON for the whole scope. `scope`, `ratchet` and `overrides` declare WHERE that policy is applied and where it is relaxed — the blind spot pass 3 exists to close was that a gate-tier ruleset was proven SELECTED but never proven APPLIED. Together they must partition CODE_ROOTS (scripts/check_structure.py): a code root is either type-checked or an explicit, costed rung. tests/integration/test_gate_scope.py enforces the partition and the pyproject/scope parity today; check_M has read `overrides` since pass 3.6 (see the bound stated there); `scope` and `ratchet` still have no consumer inside check_M itself, and teaching it to read them is the natural next rung, belonging to whoever owns check_structure.py.

overrides._comment: Declared mirror of every [[tool.mypy.overrides]] block in pyproject.toml: which module pattern may relax which flags. Until pass 3.6 check_M read only `tool.mypy.<flag>`, while _toml_targets normalises override blocks to `tool.mypy.overrides.<flag>` — so a per-module `strict = false`, an `ignore_errors = true`, or (the real case here) switching off strict's COMPONENTS was a loosening the parity gate could not see, and the blocks aliased onto one dotted key so only the last would have been read anyway. Now enforced, with a bound worth stating plainly: check_M errors on an undeclared per-module relaxation of a flag THIS ruleset declares (`strict`, the twelve components `--strict` expands to, `warn_unreachable`) or of `ignore_errors`. Keys outside that set are recorded here but NOT read by the gate — `ignore_missing_imports` on `aad` scopes import resolution rather than type strictness — so they are declared for completeness and judged by review, not by exit code. The removal condition for each lives beside the block in pyproject.toml — deleting a flag from both files is the ratchet step.

ratchet._comment: Code roots NOT yet in [tool.mypy] files. `errors` is the measured full-strict backlog. Reproduce with: MYPYPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m mypy --explicit-package-bases <root> (for `runtimes`, lift its ignore_errors override in pyproject first, or you measure 0 and learn nothing). Measured 2026-09-02: tests 958, scripts 528, runtimes 87, api 43, mcp 18. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE NUMBERS: the intent is that they only ever go down, but NOTHING ENFORCES IT — tests and scripts had drifted UP (622->958 and 464->528) with the gate green throughout, because these are declarations, not assertions. Re-measure before relying on one. Making the direction a real gate needs a test that runs mypy per pending root, which costs minutes of wall clock and is therefore its own decision. A root at zero belongs in `scope`, not here.

tests.removed_when: the test suite is annotated; blocked first on the roots it imports (disallow_untyped_calls fires in the CALLER), so this is the LAST rung, not the first

scripts.removed_when: the gate scripts are annotated — constrained by the 3.6-safe five (check_structure/check_generic/check_practices/check_python_version/generate_aad_schema), which cannot use PEP 585/604 or `from __future__ import annotations` and so need typing.List/Optional forms

runtimes.removed_when: the engine internals are annotated and runtimes/contracts.py parameterises the step state/update dicts (that one contract change also unblocks the agents.* disallow_any_generics rung)

api.removed_when: the FastAPI adapters are annotated AND api/grpc becomes checkable — its thing_pb2/thing_pb2_grpc are `make gen` output that does not exist in a fresh checkout, and grpc ships no stubs

mcp.removed_when: agents/wiki_navigator is annotated (mcp's untyped-call errors are REPORTED in mcp but CAUSED there) . The second half of this rung is DONE: mcp/protocol.py no longer passes `params.get('name')` into a `str` parameter — it validates at the transport boundary and answers -32602 invalid params (tests/unit/mcp/test_protocol.py)

practices.title: Declare element types on dict/list/set (no bare generics)
practices.mechanism: mypy disallow_any_generics
practices.subject: code

practices.title: No implicit Optional / no Optional-as-silent-failure
practices.mechanism: mypy no_implicit_optional + strict_optional; ruff RET
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Don't return Any from a typed function
practices.mechanism: mypy warn_return_any
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Every function is fully typed (no untyped defs / calls / decorators)
practices.mechanism: mypy strict (disallow_untyped_defs + disallow_incomplete_defs + disallow_untyped_calls + disallow_untyped_decorators) — Slice 5
practices.subject: code

practices.title: No blanket # noqa / # type: ignore — every suppression names its code
practices.mechanism: ruff PGH003/PGH004 — Slice 5 (pairs with the # practice-ok discipline)
practices.subject: code

practices.title: One machine-decided layout — no hand-formatting arguments in review
practices.mechanism: ruff format --check over CODE_ROOTS, via `make fmt-check` riding `make lint` (`make fmt` rewrites). Read-only in the gate: a check that writes is not a check. Formatter DEFAULTS on purpose — a configured formatter is a style opinion to re-litigate, and the point of this tier is that nobody argues. Note it reflows CODE only, so the deliberate E501 deferral for long docstring summaries is unaffected
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Every module carries the machine-readable header (title:/summary:) the corpus reads; every exported symbol is docstringed
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_O (module header; grammar pinned to build_corpus by test) + check_E (symbol docstrings, ERR since ADR-0008) + check_corpus.py (the local corpus agents query is gated fresh-when-present, stale names make site-data)
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Optimize for the reader (human or agent): readability and loud failure modes outrank speed
practices.mechanism: docs/guides/python-style.md section 0 — judgment, deliberately ungated: a heuristic gate would reject correct code. Speed is traded only with a measurement cited in a comment
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Distinguish absent (say so, continue) from broken (fail loudly) — never collapse the two
practices.mechanism: docs/guides/python-style.md section 3 — the recurring house split (openapi --check, check_corpus local gate, tests/optional_deps.py); partially gated by ruff BLE001/B904, the split itself is design judgment
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Preserve the cause; never blind-except
practices.mechanism: ruff B904 (raise ... from) + BLE001 (blind except)
practices.subject: code

practices.title: An ABC declares at least one @abstractmethod
practices.mechanism: ruff B024 + mypy abstract-instantiation
practices.subject: code

practices.title: No print() in library code; no f-string/%/+ interpolation inside log calls
practices.mechanism: ruff T20 + G + LOG (bans the anti-pattern; does NOT mandate a specific logging library)
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Public API via __init__/__all__; no cross-package _private import
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_C/check_D/check_E + ruff I
practices.subject: code

practices.title: assert_never in the default branch of Literal/Enum routing
practices.mechanism: typing.assert_never — enforced by existing mypy (Never-narrowing); convention, use it
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Don't leak a third-party exception type across a package's public boundary
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_J — flags raising an exception TYPE imported from a foreign (non-local, non-stdlib) module; builtins/relative/owned imports pass
practices.subject: code

practices.title: A declared config/settings class is frozen (immutable)
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_K — keyed on a DECLARED marker (tokens.config_marker), not a *Config name suffix
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Inject collaborators; don't construct a concrete backend inline in a doer
practices.mechanism: check_practices.py smell over tokens.provider_constructors (over/under-flags, so advisory)
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Prefer functools.singledispatch to a long isinstance chain
practices.mechanism: check_practices.py smell: >=3 isinstance branches on one subject
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Give a marked hot-path class __slots__ / dataclass(slots=True)
practices.mechanism: check_practices.py smell, gated on a `# hot-path` marker
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Annotate tensor params with a shape (jaxtyping / alias), not a bare Tensor
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_L over tokens.tensor_base_types — WARN (not err): a heuristic that over/under-flags (fires only when the cuda profile is on)
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Model graph state with TypedDict/Pydantic, not a loose dict
practices.mechanism: convention + mypy once the state type is declared
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Wrap acquire-prone resources (CUDA memory, sessions) in a context manager
practices.mechanism: check_practices.py smell over tokens.acquire_apis (fires only when the cuda profile is on)
practices.subject: code

practices.title: Every `##`-annotated make target is listed by `make help`
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_P — the help recipe's own grep pattern, read from the Makefile
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: Every relative link and `§N` citation resolves
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_Q — a closed citation grammar shared with build_corpus
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: The check catalogue and the triggers agree on one membership
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_R
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: A README declaring `## What ships here` names every member, with a `Not for` cell per row
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_S; the cell's truth is judgment (doc-style.md §2)
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: A tool spec's seven sections in order, its effect word, its `- NOT` line
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_F (body half)
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: A replaced document names its successor
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_A — `deprecated` and `superseded` both require `superseded_by`
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: `updated:` means touched: never earlier than the last commit, today when modified
practices.mechanism: scripts/review_docs.py, gated by tests/integration/test_doc_freshness.py
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: Every practice's `enforced_by` names a mechanism that exists
practices.mechanism: check_structure.py check_T
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: A backticked repository path that resolves to nothing
practices.mechanism: scripts/review_docs.py under `make advise` — advisory because most are bare basenames used as nouns
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: One checkable claim per sentence; the mechanism named; measurements dated
practices.mechanism: docs/guides/doc-style.md §4 — judgment
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: Plain imperative by default; BCP 14 keywords only in a declared specification
practices.mechanism: docs/guides/doc-style.md §5 — a `normative:` frontmatter key is designed and deferred
practices.subject: docs

practices.title: Say which idempotency property is meant, and how it is proven
practices.mechanism: docs/guides/doc-style.md §6
practices.subject: docs

tokens._comment: DATA the future AST checks/advisories match against. Listing a vendor's class name here is data, not a baked-in dependency — the checks stay vendor-neutral by reading this list (CONVENTIONS section 18). Extend per project.

profiles._comment: Domain profiles ship DEFINED but OFF. A consuming repo turns one on in project.json practices.profiles (Slice 4); until then the domain checks above never fire, so the universal template stays domain-neutral. A profile's `tags` scope its checks to corpus nodes carrying those tags — the graph tells the checker where a domain rule is even relevant.
